Maren Vane.narrative: I have set bones and eased coughs in this room behind the fish market for thirty years, and I know the quay's aches better than the Warden does. My son Ostrander is right that the lower quay cannot wait for a seawall that may never be paid for — I have seen what the tide does — but I will not say so where Mara Quell can hear me. I keep my mouth shut and my door open, and I mend what the sea and the stone leave broken.

memories.gist: The Surge came in the night and took the lower quay; I spent until dawn setting bones in the fish market with seawater to my knees.
Ostrander dragged salvage timber up from the shore and patched the lower quay himself; I bound his hands after and told him to be careful of the Warden.
Rennick came back from the fish road with a cut from a wolf and would not sit still for the stitching.
I strapped Ilse Ostrander's knees through a bad winter and she fed me noodles for a month after, which I did not refuse.
I bought salves from the Tanglewood woman at the fish market and asked her what she put in them; she would not say, and they worked.

stances.why: A healer's room has no quarrel in it; I have stitched guards and smugglers alike.
Patched shelter is better than none, whatever the Warden's plan says.
Mara Quell speaks for the quay, and my room stands on her goodwill.
The coughs come every year and the Tanglewood woman's salves are the only thing that eases them.

Maren Vane.secret: I have told Ostrander plainly that I think the Warden is wrong to hold the lower quay back, and that if it comes to a quarrel at the stalls I will stand with my son.

Rennick Vane.narrative: I walk the fish road with the runners and keep the peace at the stalls, and I have seen enough of the road to know what a man does when he is afraid. Kai Ostrander did not run from cowardice — I have carried the same fear myself on the night watch — and I will not have him called a deserter in my hearing. My mother thinks I am too ready to say what I think; my brother thinks I am too slow to say it. Both of them are wrong, and both of them are family.

memories.gist: The Surge took the lower quay in the night; I pulled two men out of the water and lost a third I could not reach.
Kai Ostrander and I stood the night watch together before the Surge, and he was the calmest man on the quay when the wind got up.
I walked Juno Reyes up the fish road through a pack of wolves and we came through with the fish and the stone both.
My mother bound a gash on my arm from a road wolf and told me I was a fool to walk it alone; I walked it again the next night.
I broke up a quarrel at the morning stalls between two fishers over a net, and both of them cursed me for it equally, which I took as fair.

stances.why: I stood the watch with him; fear does not make a coward of a man who does his duty.
The runners carry the quay's living up and down that road, and the wolves do not wait.
She pays my wage, but she is not always right, and I will not be her hand against my brother.
A guard who steps in too early makes two quarrels where there was one.

Rennick Vane.secret: I have told no one but my mother that I think Kai Ostrander ran because he was ordered to do something he would not do, and that if he came back to the quay I would hear him out before I raised a spear.
